Rhodes
ROADZ
proper noun / place
From Greek Rhodos, the great island and city of the southern Aegean; Paul’s company reached Rhodes the day after Coos (Acts 21:1).

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Rhodes is the island and harbor on the day-following after Coos, before Patara, in Paul’s launch from the elders of Ephesus toward Phenicia (Acts 21:1). The name is famous in the ancient world for ships and trade, yet Luke mentions it only as a link in the chain of obedience. That restraint is itself instructive. Scripture does not flatter tourist fame; it tracks the apostle. Rhodes becomes holy not by pagan colossus or commercial renown, but by bearing for a day the men who carried the gospel toward Jerusalem. The church learns here to measure places by the presence of Christ’s servants, not by the world’s monuments. After tears at Miletus, the company runs a clean coastal sequence: Coos, Rhodes, Patara, then a Phenician ship. Rhodes is the middle bead on that string. Ignore it, and you begin to treat Acts as a sermon anthology with scenic backdrops. Keep it, and you keep a voyage that really happened under the Lord who numbers the isles as a little thing and still writes their names when His servants sleep there. The name stands in Scripture so that the church will not invent a thinner story than the one God wrote in places and persons under providence.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Southern Aegean island; day-stop after Coos and before Patara on Paul’s voyage (Acts 21:1).

expand to see more

RHODES, a major island and city of the southern Aegean.

Paul’s company came thither the day after Coos.

From Rhodes they went on unto Patara.

The island is a commercial power in the ancient world, but a waypoint in Acts.

It belongs to the post-Miletus coastal chain toward Phenicia.

📖 Key Scripture

Acts 21:1 — "And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:"

Acts 21:2 — "And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth."

Acts 21:3 — "Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden."

Acts 20:38 — "Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Rhodes is absorbed into tourist antiquity; Luke marks it as a day of gospel travel, not a monument tour.

expand to see more

The corruption is to let pagan fame outshout the text. Rhodes becomes Colossus trivia. Scripture answers with one sober line of voyage. Recover that line and recover humility before the word’s priorities.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. What must be recovered is the plain geography and providence of Scripture: God names places so His people will remember where He acted, judged, and saved. Do not dissolve the map into mood. Hold the place, and hold the LORD who rules it.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Rhodes is the mid-island between Coos and Patara on the road from Miletus toward Phenicia.

expand to see more

Greek — Rhodos, island of the southern Aegean.

Sequence — after Coos, before Patara.

Setting — post-Miletus launch toward Syria.

Fame — trade island; gospel waypoint.

Doctrine — places measured by Christ’s servants.

Usage

"The day following they came unto Rhodes."

"From Rhodes they went on unto Patara."

"Rhodes stands mid-chain between Coos and Phenicia."
